correctness.rationale: The vertices are weighted suffix indicators because y_i=x_i/s_i lies in the order simplex 0≤y_1≤⋯≤y_n≤1. Gaussian exposure of v_k equals S_n−S_k with S_j=Σ_{i≤j}s_iG_i; thus J_n is the unique discrete minimum. Backward negative and forward positive partial-sum conditions use disjoint increments, so probabilities exactly factor; symmetric iid Sparre Andersen gives 4^(−n)binom(2k,k)binom(2n−2k,n−k). For s_i=i^α, independent Gaussian sums are precisely Brownian B(A_j), A_j=Σ i^{2α}, in finite-dimensional law. As α≥−1/2 the normalized time mesh vanishes; unique Brownian minimum U~arcsine transforms under A_j/A_n~(j/n)^{2α+1} (supercritical) or H_j/H_n~log(j+1)/log n (critical). For α<−1/2 the Gaussian series converges almost surely; its tails cannot eventually keep one sign by tail zero-one and Gaussian symmetry, ensuring the global discrete minimum is attained at a unique finite j and J_n stabilizes. Independent exact n=2 normal-cone formula checked against 120,000 fresh Gaussian draws at five exponents; limit statements depend on Brownian/zero-one proof, not these draws.
residual_risks: The same-Brownian coupling for each fixed n gives distributional statements for α≥−1/2; the almost-sure eventual index assertion for α<−1/2 uses original infinite Gaussian coupling separately.
Sparre Andersen requires continuous symmetric iid increments for equal weights only; arbitrary inhomogeneous weights use exact persistence factorization, not universal iid survival values.
